hints: Let $X$ be the number of the 20 students who use social media. Under $\text{H}_0$, $p = 0.95$, so $X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.95)$. Arvin suspects the percentage is **less**, so the rejection region is a lower tail: $X \leqslant c$ for some $c$.
The significance level is 2%. You want the largest $c$ such that $\text{P}(X \leqslant c) \leqslant 0.02$, found by working out $\text{P}(X \leqslant c)$ for values of $c$ using $\text{B}(20, 0.95)$.
Test two neighbouring values: $\text{P}(X \leqslant 17)$ and $\text{P}(X \leqslant 16)$. Use the binomial cdf on your calculator, or $1 - \text{P}(X \geqslant c + 1)$.
Compare each with 0.02: the region includes $c$ only if its probability is at most 2%. Write the rejection region as $X \leqslant c$ using the largest $c$ that passes.
walkthrough:
**Set up the test**

Let $p$ be the probability that a year 12 student at Arvin's college uses social media. The national value is 95%, and Arvin suspects his college is *lower*:

$$\text{H}_0: p = 0.95 \qquad \text{H}_1: p < 0.95$$

There are 20 students, each either uses social media or does not, independently, with the same probability. So if $\text{H}_0$ is true, the number $X$ who use it is $X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.95)$.

Because $\text{H}_1$ says *less*, a small value of $X$ is evidence against $\text{H}_0$. So the rejection region is of the form $X \leqslant c$.

**The principle for finding $c$ (this earns the first M1)**

The significance level is 2%. We want the rejection region to be as large as possible without its total probability (under $\text{H}_0$) going above 2%. So we work out cumulative probabilities $\text{P}(X \leqslant n)$ using $\text{B}(20, 0.95)$ and compare each with $0.02$.

**Calculate $\text{P}(X \leqslant 17)$ and $\text{P}(X \leqslant 16)$ (this earns the second M1 and the first A1)**

On a calculator use binomial cdf with $n = 20$, $p = 0.95$. Without that, work from the top end, where the probabilities are easiest, using $\text{P}(X = r) = \binom{20}{r}\,0.95^r\,0.05^{20-r}$:

$$\text{P}(X = 20) = 0.95^{20} = 0.35849$$

$$\text{P}(X = 19) = 20 \times 0.95^{19} \times 0.05 = 0.37735$$

$$\text{P}(X = 18) = 190 \times 0.95^{18} \times 0.05^2 = 0.18868$$

Add them: $\text{P}(X \geqslant 18) = 0.92452$, so

$$\text{P}(X \leqslant 17) = 1 - 0.92452 = 0.0755$$

Next, $\text{P}(X = 17) = 1140 \times 0.95^{17} \times 0.05^3 = 0.05958$, so

$$\text{P}(X \leqslant 16) = 0.07548 - 0.05958 = 0.0159$$

The scheme also accepts the equivalent complements: $\text{P}(X \geqslant 18) = 0.925$ and $\text{P}(X \geqslant 17) = 0.984$.

**Compare with 2% (this earns the last A1)**

$\text{P}(X \leqslant 17) = 0.0755$, and $0.0755 > 0.02$, so 17 is **not** in the rejection region.

$\text{P}(X \leqslant 16) = 0.0159$, and $0.0159 < 0.02$, so 16 **is** in the rejection region.

So the largest value that fits is 16. The scheme withholds the last A1 unless both probabilities are shown, so write them both.

hints: A Type I error is rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when $\text{H}_0$ is actually true. So it is the probability of landing in your rejection region from (a) while $p = 0.95$.
walkthrough:
**What a Type I error is**

A Type I error happens when we reject $\text{H}_0$ even though $\text{H}_0$ is true. Here $\text{H}_0$ says $p = 0.95$. If it is true, $X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.95)$, and we wrongly reject if $X$ falls in the rejection region $X \leqslant 16$.

$$\text{P}(\text{Type I error}) = \text{P}(X \leqslant 16 \mid p = 0.95)$$

We already found this in part (a):

$$\text{P}(X \leqslant 16) = 0.0159$$

Quick check: it is a bit below the 2% level we were given. That is expected, because $X$ is discrete, so we cannot hit 2% exactly.

hints: A Type II error is not rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when it is actually false. Jimmy says the true $p$ is 0.7, so now $X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.7)$.
You fail to reject when $X$ is **outside** the rejection region from (a), i.e. $X > 16$. Write $\text{P}(X > 16)$ for $\text{B}(20, 0.7)$.
Either use $1 - \text{P}(X \leqslant 16)$ on the calculator, or add the probabilities for $X = 17, 18, 19, 20$ with $p = 0.7$. Give 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**What a Type II error is (this earns the first M1)**

A Type II error happens when $\text{H}_0$ is false but we do not reject it. Assume Jimmy is right and the true value is $p = 0.7$. Then the number of students using social media is

$$X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.7)$$

**Write the probability (this earns the second M1)**

We do **not** reject $\text{H}_0$ when $X$ is outside the rejection region $X \leqslant 16$. That means $X \geqslant 17$, which is $X > 16$:

$$\text{P}(\text{Type II error}) = \text{P}(X > 16 \mid p = 0.7) = \text{P}(X \geqslant 17)$$
